_readme: Hand corrections for bags/generate_category2_qa.py, applied on every run so the
benchmark stays reproducible from the metadata rather than hand-edited afterwards.
Rules are keyed by question text (case- and period-insensitive), not by question id,
so renumbering cannot silently move a correction onto a different question.
pin:    official question text -> object id. Use when the text solver reports the
question unresolved: several objects satisfy it, the winner is inside the
0.30 m margin, or the object it names is missing from the metadata. The id
comes from reading the screenshot the PDF shows beside the question, where
the expected answer is outlined, against <scene>_objects.json.
reword: question text -> replacement text. Phrasing only; it must still name the
same object, since the answer box is not re-derived from the new wording.
drop:   list of question texts to exclude. Generated questions are backfilled from
the candidate pool, so a scene still lands on 10.
note:   question text -> a note carried into the QA file as review_note.

note.Find the bowl on the table closest to th: The painted folding screen is not an object in the metadata, so the anchor cannot be resolved automatically. Both bowls sit on table 88; bowl 91 is the one nearer the screen and the one outlined in the PDF screenshot.

drop: Find the curtain that is closest to the camera.
Find the chair that is closest to the camera.

note.Find the ceiling lamp that is farthest f: Backfilled after dropping two questions anchored on camera 46: a 13 cm photo camera is a confusing landmark to name in a robot benchmark, where 'the camera' reads as the robot's own.

No object is labelled sushi; the sushi sits on dish 33. Pillow 46 is the closest of the four maroon floor pillows to that dish (0.42 m) and the one outlined in the PDF screenshot.

Find the vase with the flower in it.

Same object, natural phrasing: the flower's stems rise above the vase's rim, which the metadata records as the vase being below the flower.

note.Find the pillow on the sofa that is clos: Centre-to-centre distance ties sofa 71 against couch 24 in the other region. The question is about sofa 71: pillow 39 touches lamp 81 and is the black-heart cushion outlined in the PDF screenshot.

note.The blue chair that is closest to the cu: Chair 99 wins under both metrics (0.51 m centre, 0.05 m box-gap) but by less than the 0.30 m margin, because the chairs are only 0.70 m apart. The PDF screenshot outlines the middle near-side chair, which is chair 99.

note.Find the box on the cabinet that is clos: Cabinet 160 is 0.21 m from whiteboard 113 but its centre distance ties with cabinet 155 across the room. Box 36 is the one resting on cabinet 160, next to the phone, as outlined in the PDF screenshot.
